A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FUTURIST and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding methods, experiments, and qualitative examples can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original Cityscapes segmentation and depth forecasting results, component ablations, computational comparisons, and qualitative rollouts.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds evaluations involving fine-tuned VISTA and LDM tokenizers.

M1.justification: The hierarchical tokenizer, modality fusion, masking strategies, transformer, decoder, and training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix C's instance-offset representation is a suggested future extension, not an implemented change to FUTURIST.

E1.justification: Both versions use Cityscapes for semantic segmentation and depth forecasting, including the same long-horizon qualitative scenarios. Baseline fine-tuning uses retained coverage; instance and panoptic segmentation remain future work.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 6 replace pretrained VISTA with Cityscapes-fine-tuned VISTA. Table 7 adds an LDM VQ-VAE-FT forecasting variant and its reconstruction oracle. The other forecasting methods and component comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a 10-epoch Cityscapes LoRA fine-tuning protocol for VISTA and modality-specific fine-tuning for the LDM tokenizer. FUTURIST's data splits, forecasting horizons, metrics, architecture settings, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds controls examining whether adaptation addresses VISTA's domain mismatch and the tokenizer comparison's modality mismatch; v1 explicitly left tokenizer retraining outside scope. V2 also adds tokenizer-related efficiency comparisons. Existing fusion, masking, sequence-length, and rollout analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. V2 retains the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Baseline findings change substantially. Tables 1 and 6 replace VISTA's short/mid-term ALL mIoU of 45.7/40.4 with fine-tuned results of 65.7/53.2, now exceeding Copy-Last in all segmentation columns. These involve different training conditions. Table 7 adds LDM-FT forecasting results of 69.2/57.2 and reconstruction mIoU of 77.1. Appendix A.2 adds efficiency measurements. FUTURIST scores remain unchanged; Table 6 also corrects Copy-Last values from 55.6 to 55.5 and 32.3 to 32.2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of tokenization, fusion, masking, and decoding, together with loss Equations 1–2, retain the same substance. No theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a VAE-free multimodal transformer, cross-modal prediction benefits, efficient end-to-end training, and state-of-the-art Cityscapes semantic forecasting. The added comparisons support existing claims rather than redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces the dismissal of tokenizer retraining as outside scope with discussion of fine-tuning and efficiency tradeoffs. Appendix C adds a concrete prospective extension using instance-center offsets. The conclusion drops its subtle-visual-detail caveat, while action-conditioning and long-horizon limitations remain documented.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies full-resolution evaluation, VISTA's LoRA fine-tuning resources and batch size, and tokenizer comparison parameter counts, training times, and inference latency. The abstract changes the access pointer from a direct code repository to a project-and-code page. Full-resolution evaluation is newly disclosed, not established as a changed setting.

R1.justification: Related work expands to additional panoptic forecasting studies and an additional F2MF reference. The proposed future extension cites instance and panoptic segmentation approaches including PersonLab and ViP-DeepLab. The paper's central positioning relative to prior methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: updated affiliation and access text, standardized headings and cross-references, expanded related-work and appendix passages, and a shortened conclusion. The overall section organization and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 7 gains two fine-tuned rows. Tables 1–2 and Figure 5 are repositioned within page 7, with associated text and appendix reflow. Existing diagrams and qualitative figures are retained; the qualitative image content is identical.

improvement.justification: The adapted VISTA and LDM comparisons address weaknesses in v1's reliance on pretrained baselines, strengthening evidence for FUTURIST's retained advantages. Added implementation and efficiency details improve transparency. However, interpretation was not fully reconciled with the new evidence: Section 4.2 still says VISTA performs below Copy-Last, directly contradicting revised Tables 1 and 6. The net improvement is therefore limited.
